manifest.summary: Command-line arguments move into a ripgrep-specific definition model, repeatable value-taking flags select their last supplied value, and positional names become internally consistent.

items.title: Define each command-line argument through a local model
items.before: The clap application was assembled as one inline chain using shared closures and clap settings.
items.after: RGArg and RGArgKind describe positional arguments, switches, and value-taking flags, while per-argument functions keep each definition with its help text.
items.statement: The application is generated from ripgrep-owned argument descriptions that are then translated to clap.

items.title: Use the last value of a repeated value-taking flag
items.before: ArgMatches exposed clap singleton accessors, whose repeated-value lookup selected clap's singleton result.
items.after: The wrapper owns singleton access and derives it from all supplied values by taking the last value.
items.statement: Consumers such as replacement, color, and encoding read through the wrapper's last-value semantics.

items.title: Use normalized internal names for pattern and path positionals
items.before: Argument consumption referred to PATTERN and PATH using uppercase identifiers.
items.after: Argument consumption refers to the model's lowercase pattern and path identifiers.
items.statement: Path and pattern extraction now uses the identifiers emitted by the new argument model.
